To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
preoperative TACE is a safe procedure that does not increase the operative risk for liver transplantation.

TACE does not offer a survival advantage when used as a neoadjunt therapy prior to OLT for HCC, and that TACE does neither allow to expand the current criteria for OLT selection, nor to decrease the dropout rate on the waiting list.
TACE does not offer any benefit when used as a bridge to OTL, nor when used prior to surgery in HCC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) Is there evidence that TACE improves long‐term outcome after OLT?
the role of TAE in the pre‐transplantation treatment of HCC patients on the waiting list for LT.
a systematic evaluation of the evidence on the impact of TACE as a bridge to O LT for HCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TACE as a bridge to O LT for HCC has no impact on long‐term survival, does not increase dropout rates on the wait‐list, and does not increase the rate of postoperative complications.
TACE does not appear to improve survival, nor to expand the current criteria of OLT, nor to decrease dropout rates on the transplant list.
TACE as a bridge to O LT is not beneficial, but not harmful either, in patients with early and advanced HCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TACE is a safe and feasible procedure in patients with HCC who are candidates for liver transplantation.
TACE is not a standard therapy for HCC before OLT.
TACE is not a recommended treatment for HCC patients who are waiting for OLT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current evidence does not support the use of TACE as a bridge to O LT for HCC patients.
the current evidence does not support the use of TACE prior to OLT.
the current evidence does not support the use of TACE as a neoadjunt therapy in HCC patients awaiting liver transplantation.
